newsitem.title: LEBANON: Six dead, 36 hurt in fierce South Lebanon shelling.
newsitem.headline: Six dead, 36 hurt in fierce South Lebanon shelling.

text.p: Six civilians were killed and 36 wounded in fierce shelling on Monday in the bloodiest attack on the port city of Sidon since a major Israeli offensive in south Lebanon in 1996.
The Israeli army said forces under the command of pro-Israeli militia leader Antoine Lahd were behind the attack.

Shortly after the shelling of Sidon, six Katyusha rockets struck Jezzine, a Lahd stronghold just outside an Israeli-held occupation zone in south Lebanon, killing a 60-year-old civilian man and wounding two women, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
Lahd is commander of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) in the occupation zone which also controls the Jezzine area.
"The SLA is backed by Israel whereas the people who fired are not backed by Israel," an Israeli military source insisted.
In Beirut, the Lebanese army issued a statement saying the shelling of Sidon, 40 km (25 miles) south of Beirut, was carried out by Israel's local militia allies in Jezzine.
The attack marked the first time that Sidon faced shelling since the end of a major Israeli military offensive in April 1996.
It came hours after an explosion in Jezzine killed two Lebanese youths.
Military sources said the shelling followed an increase in attacks on the Jezzine area, where the SLA and Iranian-backed Hizbollah guerrillas often engage in fierce clashes.
A total of 16 shells landed in Sidon and its suburbs, forcing residents to abandon the city's main road and many shops to close.
Hours after the attack the city remained tense. Ambulance sirens echoed through Sidon.
Security sources in Lebanon put the death toll at six and Sidon hospitals said the number of wounded climbed to 36, many of them seriously.
Victims were rushed to five hospitals where doctors tried to identify the dead.

"We have two heads and parts of bodies in the post-mortem room. Many people came but nobody was able to identify them. We still don't know who they belong to," said a medic at Sidon's Ghassan Hamoud hospital.
The wounded tried to make sense of the violence.

"I heard an explosion close to my door and went out to check. I suddenly found myself sinking in blood and now I am here. That's all I know," said Ibrahim Shabaan, 70, half of his head covered by a bandage.
Ten-year-old Wissam was playing soccer with his friends when a shell struck nearby.
"I was playing with my friends with a ball. A bomb hit the barber shop. It left a hole in my leg," he told Reuters.
Surgeons at a nearby hospital worked frantically to remove shrapnel from the head and body of Riad Firhal, a two-month-old boy, but feared they would not be able to save the child.
One hour after the rocket attack on Jezzine, 10 Katyusha rockets hit Marjayoun in south Lebanon, where Israeli forces in Lebanon and the SLA maintain their headquarters.
Hizbollah sources in Beirut said they had no immediate information on the attacks.
Security sources said that the Lebanese army retaliated against the Sidon shelling with artillery fire on SLA positions in Jezzine.
Hizbollah's top official in south Lebanon, Nabeel Kawouk, threatened to carry out reprisals for the shelling by pro-Israeli militias.

"We must speak in the language that the Israeli enemy understands and it is not possible to keep silent about what happened today. The enemy must understand a deeply bitter message," he told reporters after visiting some of the wounded in Sidon hospitals.
